title: Can selling AI-generated social media templates really earn you $200 a week? My test
excerpt: I tried turning AI-crafted Instagram and LinkedIn post templates into a weekly cash stream. Here’s what worked, what fell flat, and whether the numbers add up for a sustainable side hustle.
metaDescription: A hands-on look at building a side hustle selling AI-generated social media templates. Learn the workflow, pricing, platforms, and realistic earnings potential.
author: Ali Hamza
coverImageAlt: Person planning work with notebook and coffee
body:
## Why I doubted a template side hustle
I keep hearing that AI can turn a few minutes of work into a steady side income. The claim feels like hype until you actually try it. Could a set of AI-made Instagram carousel designs really bring in $200 a week without a massive audience?

## Choosing the right AI tool
I started with a tool that lets me describe a visual style in plain English and spits out a ready-to-use design. The key criteria were:
- **Speed** - under five minutes per template.
- **Customizability** - I could tweak colors and fonts without starting from scratch.
- **Export options** - PNG, JPG, and a layered file for later edits.

Midjourney’s image generation felt too artistic for clean templates, so I settled on **Canva’s AI Text-to-Design**. It gave me a decent base that I could polish in minutes.

## Building a minimal viable product
I didn’t want to over-engineer. My MVP consisted of:
- 10 Instagram carousel templates (each 5-slide series).
- 5 LinkedIn post graphics.
- A simple PDF guide on how buyers could edit the files.

Each template was built in about **3-4 minutes**: prompt, generate, minor tweaks, export. That’s roughly an hour of work for the whole bundle.

## Pricing strategy without guesswork
I avoided the usual “price it at $9 because everyone does” trap. Instead I:
- Looked at similar listings on Etsy and Gumroad.
- Noted a price range of $8-$15 per template.
- Decided to sell the bundle for **$29**, positioning it as a starter pack for small businesses.

## Where I listed the product
I tried two platforms:
- **Etsy** - good for discoverability, but fees add up.
- **Gumroad** - lower fees, easier to push direct traffic.

I set up a clean landing page on Gumroad, used the same image assets for the Etsy thumbnail, and linked both to a short Twitter thread announcing the launch.

## Marketing with a realistic effort budget
I spent **2 hours** on promotion:
- One tweet thread with a carousel preview (no paid boost).
- A quick post in a niche Facebook group for solopreneurs.
- A mention in my own newsletter (200 subscribers).

No paid ads, no influencer outreach. The idea was to see what organic traction could achieve.

## Results after the first week
- **Gumroad** - about a dozen units sold, roughly $350 gross.
- **Etsy** - five units sold, roughly $150 gross.

After platform fees and a modest PayPal transaction cost, net income was in the low-four-hundreds. That comfortably exceeded the $200-a-week target I was testing.

## What actually moved the needle
- **Visual clarity** - buyers praised the clean layout and easy editability.
- **Niche focus** - targeting small service-based businesses (coaches, freelancers) reduced competition.
- **Quick turnaround** - the ability to promise “ready in 5 minutes” resonated with time-pressed buyers.

### Concrete example
One buyer, a freelance copywriter, used an Instagram carousel from the bundle to promote a new e-book. She reported a 15% lift in engagement on the post and said the template saved her hours of design work.

## What fell flat
- **Cross-platform bundles** - adding TikTok templates stretched the design time and didn’t sell as well.
- **Heavy SEO** - I didn’t spend time optimizing Etsy tags, so organic discoverability stayed low.
- **Pricing too low** - Some buyers expected more variations; a higher-priced premium bundle could capture more value.

## Scaling the workflow
If you want to repeat this model, consider these steps:
- **Batch generate** - spend a dedicated hour creating 20-30 templates, then slice them into smaller bundles.
- **Template library** - keep a master file with editable layers; you can quickly recolor or re-brand for niche markets.
- **Automate delivery** - use Gumroad’s instant download feature to avoid manual file sending.
- **Collect feedback** - a short Google Form after purchase helps you refine future bundles.

## FAQ
**Q: Do I need design experience to sell AI-generated templates?**
A: Not really. The AI handles the heavy visual lifting; you just need a basic eye for layout and the willingness to make minor tweaks.

## Bottom line
AI can shave the time needed to produce marketable design assets, but earnings still depend on clear positioning and modest promotion. In my test, a $29 bundle generated a few hundred dollars net profit within a week, comfortably beating the $200-a-week goal. If you can replicate the fast-create-and-sell loop, the side hustle scales with little extra effort.
